commit.message:
Fix 32-bit indexing overflow in conv subsampling chunking guard (#15858)

* Fix 32-bit indexing overflow in conv subsampling chunking guard

Signed-off-by: Jeronymous <jeromelouradour@gmail.com>

* Size conv_split_by_batch chunking factor against input and output

Mirror the forward() split guard, which triggers on either the conv input or
its first-conv output reaching the 32-bit element limit, so the auto chunking
factor is computed from the larger of the two rather than the output alone.

Signed-off-by: Jeronymous <jeromelouradour@gmail.com>

* Add unit tests for conv subsampling 32-bit indexing guard

Cover the boundary fix and auto chunking factor with small synthetic inputs and
a lowered limit (via monkeypatch), so no multi-GB tensors are needed:
- _first_conv_output_numel matches the real first-conv output element count
- the guard splits at output == limit and not one element below it
- splitting (by batch, and by channel for batch size 1) preserves the result
- the auto chunking factor yields chunks strictly below the limit

Signed-off-by: Jeronymous <jeromelouradour@gmail.com>

* remove unused import

Signed-off-by: Jeronymous <jeromelouradour@gmail.com>

* Split conv subsampling by single sample when factor exceeds batch size

When the auto chunking factor rounds up past the batch size (e.g. b=3, cf=4),
b // cf was 0, so conv_split_by_batch gave up and the forward fell back to
conv_split_by_channel, which unsqueezes the batch and runs the full first conv
with the batch dimension read as channels, raising a channel-count error.

Split into batches of one instead, falling back to channel splitting only when
a single sample alone exceeds the 32-bit element limit. Add a b=3 regression
test.

Signed-off-by: Jeronymous <jeromelouradour@gmail.com>

* Trim redundant comments added in this PR

Signed-off-by: Jeronymous <jeromelouradour@gmail.com>

* Guard single sample against input numel too, not just output

Signed-off-by: Jeronymous <jeromelouradour@gmail.com>

---------

Signed-off-by: Jeronymous <jeromelouradour@gmail.com>
